newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-SUBSTITUTE RAUL LEADS REAL TO CUP VICTORY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SUBSTITUTE RAUL LEADS REAL TO CUP VICTORY.

text.p: Late goals by Predrag Mijatovic and Raul Gonzalez were enough to give Real Madrid a hard-fought third round Spanish Cup victory over Valladolid on Wednesday.
After only winning 2-1 in the first leg at home, Real were at times in some danger against this season's surprise outfit before the arrival of Raul as substitute turned round the tie.
But Cup action may have proved the final straw for two managers -- Sporting Gijon's Benito Floro and Zaragoza's Victor Esparrago, who both saw their sides crash out.
Former Real manager Floro was thought to be close to dismissal after his Sporting Gijon side could only manage a 2-2 draw against Espanyol, who ran out 6-3 winners on aggregate.
Zaragoza -- currently 21st in the league -- missed several chances and went down 1-0 at Racing Santander after drawing the first leg 1-1.
In other ties cup-specialists Athletic Bilbao came from behind to draw 2-2 at home to second division Villareal, and went through thanks to a 1-0 win in the first leg.

Rayo Vallecano recovered from a 3-2 defeat at second division Osasuna with a 3-1 win at home, while Celta Vigo's 2-0 win in the first leg was enough to see them through after the 2-2 draw at Logrones.
Compostela went through 3-1, 3-0 on the night with two goals from Bulgarian striker Lyuboslav Penev against Oviedo, who ended the game with just nine men because of sendings-off.
